senses.gloss: ch. same, to be sanctified, sacred (v. קְדוֹשׁ).
units: Shebu. 15ᵇ שתי הלחם … דקַדְשֵׁי (Rashi דמִיקַּדְּשֵׁי Ithpa.) it is through the slaughtering of the sheep that the two loaves received their sacred character.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 4b:18">Bekh. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>דקְדוּשׁ קדוש וכ׳</he> those firstborn that were consecrated, were consecrated &c.

senses.gloss: as preced. Pi., to sanctify; to proclaim; to betroth &c.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 28:41">Targ. Ex. XXVIII, 41</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 29:1">Ib. XXIX, 1</cite> <he>לקַדָּשָׁא</he> (Y. <he>לקַדְשָׁא</he>). Ib. 44; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 20:7">Targ. Y. Deut. XX, 7</cite> (not <he>דקָדֵישׁ</he>; h. text <cite ref="A03250"><he>ארש</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 22:16">Ib. XXII, 16</cite> (h. text <he>נתתי</he>); a. e.—
<cite ref="Shevuot 16a:4">Shebu. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>ועזרא קַדּוּשֵׁי ק׳ וכ׳</he> and Ezra consecrated (the various places), although the Urim and Tummim were no longer extant.

<cite ref="Pesachim 106a:6">Pes. 106ᵃ</cite> <he>עיקר קידושא … דכי ק׳ תחלת יומא בעי לקַדּוּשֵׁי</he> the actual sanctification of the Sabbath must take place in the evening, for when one sanctifies the Sabbath, one must sanctify the beginning of the day.

<cite ref="Pesachim 106a:6">Ib.</cite> <he>ליקַדֵּישׁ לן וכ׳</he> please, sir, recite for us the great Ḳiddush, v. <cite ref="S00874"><he>קִידּוּשָׁא</he></cite>. Ib. 101ᵃ <he>לקדושי בביתא</he> to recite the Ḳiddush in the house. Ib. 106ᵇ <he>זימנין … מקדש אריפתא</he> at times, when he cared more for bread, he recited the Ḳiddush over bread.—
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25a:9">R. Hash. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>זיל … וקַדְּשֵׁיה וכ׳</he> go to ‘En-Ṭab and proclaim the New Moon Day.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>אמר … בעינן לקדושי בך וכ׳</he> he said (to the moon), to-night we desire to initiate the new month through thee, and thou standest here? <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25b:12">Ib.ᵇ</cite> <he>ולִיקַדְּשֵׁיה בליליא</he> Ms. M. and we may proclaim it at night.

<cite ref="Shevuot 15b:7">Shebu. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>דעד דקַדֵּישׁ יומא וכ׳</he> so that immediately after one has recited the blessing at the exit of the day (<cite ref="E00028"><he>הַבְדָּלָה</he></cite>), one might finish the building and consecrate it.—
<cite ref="Kiddushin 50b:7">Kidd. 50ᵇ</cite> <he>באתרא דמְקַדְּשֵׁי והדר מסבלי</he> where it is customary to send the gifts after betrothal, v. <cite ref="O00072"><he>סְבַל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 59a:4">Ib. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>לקדושי … לבריה</he> to betroth a wife for his son (as his deputy); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְקַדַּשׁ</he>; f. <cite ref="M02385"><he>מְקַדְּשָׁא</he></cite>, &c. Shebu. l. c. <he>תרוייהו … מְקַדְּשֵׁי</he> both of them are consecrated at the same time. Ib. <he>חדא מי מק׳</he> how can even one of them be consecrated?—
<cite ref="Pesachim 101a:6">Pes. 101ᵃ</cite> <he>ולא מק׳ לכו בבית אכילה</he> (Ms. M. 2 <he>מתקדש</he>) and no Ḳiddush will be recited for you in your dining place; a. fr.

senses.gloss: ; Ithpe. אִיקְּדִישׁ to sanctify one’s self; to be sanctified; (of mixed seeds) to be condemnable; (of woman) to be betrothed.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 29:37">Targ. Ex. XXIX, 37</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 20:7">Targ. Lev. XX, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 10:3">Targ. O. ib. X, 3</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Kiddushin 54a:7">Kidd. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>ירושלים מי מִיקַּדְּשָׁא</he> is Jerusalem itself consecrated ground? <cite ref="Nedarim 31a:6">Ned. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון דאיק׳ אברהם וכ׳</he> when Abraham was consecrated (as the bearer of religion), they (the Israelites) were called after him (they are no longer included among ‘the sons of Noah’).—

<cite ref="Ketubot 62b:15">Keth. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>אי מִיקַּדַּשְׁנָא</he> (some ed. <he>מְקַדַּשְׁנָא</he>) if I consent to be betrothed unto thee, wilt thou go to college? <cite ref="Ketubot 62b:15">Ib.</cite> <he>אִיקַּדְּשָׁא ליה וכ׳</he> she was betrothed to him in secret, and she sent him (Akiba) away (to study).

<cite ref="Kiddushin 9a:1">Kidd. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>אי … מִיקַּדְּשַׁת לי</he> if I give it thee, wilt thou be betrothed to me? <cite ref="Kiddushin 12a:2">Ib. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>אשה … לא מִיקַּדְּשָׁא</he> a woman cannot be betrothed with a P’ruṭah; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 105a:2">Pes. 105ᵃ</cite> <he>זיל חזי אי מִקְּדִישׁ יומא</he> (Ms. M. <he>קדיש</he>) go and see whether the sacred day has begun.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 27:14">Targ. Lev. XXVII, 14</cite> (Y. ed. Vien. <he>יִקְדַּשׁ</he>). Ib. 15.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 17:3">Targ. Jud. XVII, 3</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 9b:8">Kidd. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>עד דמַקְדִּישׁ והדר בעיל</he> (Rashi <he>דמקדש</he>) until he betroth her and consummates.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 12a:14">Ib. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>ההוא גברא דא׳ וכ׳</he> a man betrothed a woman with a piece of &c., v. <cite ref="K00239"><he>כּוֹחֲלָא</he></cite>.
Ib. 12ᵇ; a. fr. (interch. with Pa.).
